text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Start of direct talks between President Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Denktash on July 9 takes form of unofficial international conference on Cyprus issue as Cyprus's guarantor powers, Security Council and European Union, will be monitoring on sidelines.
- Communist Akel and Socialist Edek have crucial meeting on Thursday which will determine fate of mooted alliance of opposition parties during presidential elections.
- Details of talks in New York on July 9 have been set.
- Man accused of infecting his lover with HIV accuses her of having weakness for unprotected sex.
- Alliance of opposition parties in presidential elections is a matter of political will, which Akel has, says general secretary Demetris Christofias.
- Parliament studies tender procedure for leasing of marinas to private sector.
- New York talks on July 9 will get off ground with submission of document by United Nations.
- Trade unions want government to extend suspension on employment of new foreign labourers until September 30, but employers insist that it be valid only until June 30.
- Clerides and Denktash will be isolated in New York. United Nations trying to create "friendly" climate.
